source.primary_witnesses: Aramaic DSS fragments (4Q201-4Q207; late 3rd c. BCE through 1st c. BCE) where preserved; Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus (6th c. CE) where Aramaic absent; Ge'ez (medieval; the only complete witness) as fallback
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly conventions: Aramaic Imperial-Aramaic transliteration per Milik 1976 (ḥ ṣ ʿ ḫ); Greek SBL convention (η→ē, ω→ō, θ→th, etc., matching Matthew precedent); Ge'ez SBL Ge'ez convention (ḫ ḫ̣ ʾ ʿ ä for ä-vowel)
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Milik 1976 DJD apparatus + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia + original codicology
source.fetchedFrom: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch + Black 1985 Greek text + Charles 1912 Ge'ez PD + Knibb 1978 Ge'ez critical edition + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia commentary
source.citation: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch (Oxford); Black 1985 The Book of Enoch or 1 Enoch (SVTP 7, Leiden); Nickelsburg 2001 1 Enoch 1 Hermeneia; Charles 1912 The Book of Enoch (Oxford, PD); Knibb 1978 The Ethiopic Book of Enoch (Oxford); Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 DJD XXXVI; VanderKam 1984 Enoch and the Growth of an Apocalyptic Tradition; Reed 2005 Fallen Angels.
source.paleography_note: The layered-witness convention reflects the manuscript-attestation reality: Aramaic DSS fragments are FRAGMENTARY (preserve only portions of chs 1-36); Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus preserves chs 1-32 substantially complete; Ge'ez is the only complete witness but the most distant in time and language from the Aramaic original. Per-verse selection prioritizes the oldest preserved witness; alternate witnesses documented where they differ materially or provide cross-collation value.

verses.text: ואסאל אלף לאנשא למעבד סיפין וסכינין ואספרא ומחלצין ואחזי אנון מטמורה ולתכלי כספא ודהבא וכל מן אבן יקרא וצבעיא וכל סממניא ואשתנו

verses.text_greek: Ἀζαὴλ δὲ ἐδίδαξεν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ποιεῖν μαχαίρας καὶ ὅπλα καὶ ἀσπίδας καὶ θώρακας, καὶ ἐδήλωσεν αὐτοῖς τὰ μέταλλα καὶ τὴν ἐργασίαν αὐτῶν, καὶ ψέλια καὶ κόσμους καὶ στιβίοις, καὶ τὸ καλλιβλέφαρον, καὶ παντοίους λίθους ἐκλεκτοὺς καὶ τὰ βαφικά.
verses.text_geez: ወአዜኤል፡ መሀሮሙ፡ ለሰብእ፡ ግቢረ፡ መጣብኅት፡ ወመቅሰፍት፡ ወሰይፋት፡ ወድርዓታት፡ ወሥራዓታት፡ ወአርአዮሙ፡ ቊፀረ፡ ብሩር፡ ወወርቅ፡ ወአርአዮሙ፡ ዘመረ፡ ወዘይከዐው፡ ላዕሌሁ፡ ወአምዕዝ፡ ወአዕናቍ፡ ወአልባበ፡ ቆንጅዋን፡ ወማዕይባተ፡ ቅብዓት፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q201 1 iv 1-3 + 4Q202 1 iii 1-5 (Milik 1976 pp. 157-160, 167-170) — Aramaic preserves the Asael name + the knowledge-catalog opening
verses.notes: **MAJOR LENS-RISK + CANON-ENGAGEMENT SITE — THE ASAEL KNOWLEDGE-TRANSMISSION CATALOG.** This is the central canon-interest site per Yes... I am Raelian: Asael (אסאל / Ἀζαήλ / Azazel) teaches humanity (1) metallurgy — making swords (סיפין), knives (סכינין), shields (אספרא), breastplates (מחלצין); (2) mining/metalworking — silver, gold; (3) precious stones; (4) cosmetics — antimony/eye-paint, bracelets, ornaments; (5) dyes. **The Aramaic 4Q201 reads ʾAsʾēl (אסאל)**; the Greek Akhmim reads Ἀζαὴλ (Azael), which becomes 'Azazel' in later transmission — the connection to the Lev 16 Yom Kippur scapegoat sent 'to Azazel' (לעזאזל) is one of the cruxes of the canon-engagement (Reed 2005; Nickelsburg 2001 pp. 191-194). **Cross-corpus**: the apkallū tradition (Mesopotamian seven sages teaching humanity crafts) — Adapa, Oannes, Berossus' antediluvian sages. Cross-corpus to Prometheus (Greek titan teaching humans metallurgy + fire). **LENS-RISK / CANON-ENGAGEMENT**: this verse is the Watchers-as-Elohim-technology-bringers reading-site. The Asael narrative (Watcher teaches weapons + metallurgy + cosmetics + astronomy = the foundational technical-civilizational knowledge) is the canon's central textual interest in 1 Enoch. Acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework applies — the text presents this knowledge-transfer ambivalently (corrupting humanity in v. 2). Editor will handle the framing carefully.

verses.text_greek: καὶ ἐγένετο ἀσέβεια πολλὴ καὶ ἐπόρνευσαν, καὶ ἐπλανήθησαν καὶ ἠφανίσθησαν ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai egeneto asebeia pollē kai eporneusan, kai eplanēthēsan kai ēphanisthēsan en pasi tois hodois autōn.
verses.text_geez: ወኮነ፡ ረሲዕ፡ ብዙኅ፡ ወዘመዉ፡ ወስሕቱ፡ ወሐስው፡ በኵሉ፡ ፍናዊሆሙ፡
verses.notes: The moral consequence of the knowledge-transfer: humanity becomes impious, sexually corrupt, deceived. The Greek triad of asebeia / porneuō / planaō / aphanizō structures the indictment as a cascade. Editor: this is the framing-pivot — the texts presents knowledge-transfer as morally negative.

verses.text: שמיחזה אלף חרשין ולקטעת שרשין חרמני אלף שריות חרשין ברקאל אלף נחשי ברקין כוכבאל נחשי כוכבין זקיאל נחשי זיקין שמשיאל נחשי שמשא שהריאל נחשי סהרא
verses.translit: Šĕmīḥăzāh ʾallēp ḥăršīn wĕ-lě-qiṭʿat šoršīn, Ḥarmōnī ʾallēp šărāyōt ḥăršīn, Bărāqʾēl ʾallēp něḥăšē bĕrāqīn, Kōkabʾēl něḥăšē kōkabīn, Zīqīʾēl něḥăšē zīqīn, Šamšīʾēl něḥăšē šimšāʾ, Šaḥrīʾēl něḥăšē sahărāʾ
verses.text_greek: Ἀμηζαρὰκ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐπαοιδοῖς καὶ ῥιζοτόμοις, Ἀρμαρὼς λυτηρίους τῶν ἐπαοιδῶν, Βαρακιὴλ τοὺς ἀστρολόγους, Κωκαβιὴλ τὰ σημειωτικὰ, καὶ Τάμιὴλ τὰς ἀστρολογίας ἐδίδαξαν, καὶ Ἀσραδὴλ τὴν ὁδὸν τῆς σελήνης.
verses.text_geez: ሰማይዓዛ፡ መሀረ፡ ሥራዬ፡ ወመሰብርተ፡ ሥሮታት፡ አርማርስ፡ ፈትሐ፡ ሥራይ፡ በራቅያል፡ ኮከበ፡ ሰማይ፡ ኮካባኤል፡ ተአምራት፡ ወአዜራኤል፡ ጽዮኖት፡ ወአራቅያል፡ ምልክተ፡ ምድር፡ ሰምሳፒኤል፡ ምልክተ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወሰርያኤል፡ ምልክተ፡ ወርኅ፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q201 1 iv 5-8 + 4Q202 1 iii 6-12 (Milik 1976 pp. 157-160, 167-172) — KEY Aramaic preservation of the Watcher-specialty assignments
verses.notes: **MAJOR LENS-RISK + CANON-ENGAGEMENT SITE.** **The Watcher-specialty assignments — distinct knowledge-domains.** Šemiḥazah teaches enchantments + root-cutting (pharmacological magic). Ḥarmōnī (Aramaic; Greek Ἀρμαρώς) teaches dissolution-of-enchantments. **Bărāqʾēl teaches divination from lightning** (něḥăšē bĕrāqīn — lightning-omens). **Kōkabʾēl teaches astrology** (něḥăšē kōkabīn — star-divination). **Zīqīʾēl teaches shooting-star-divination.** **Šamšīʾēl teaches solar-divination.** **Šaḥrīʾēl teaches lunar-divination.** The Watcher specialties = the cosmic-divination disciplines. The Aramaic preserves the catalog more clearly than the corrupted Greek (which collapses some specialties). **CROSS-CORPUS**: the Mesopotamian apkallū are explicitly the teachers of celestial-divination (cf. the Babylonian Enuma Anu Enlil omen-series); cf. Berossus on the antediluvian-sages teaching all arts. The Watchers as the Hebrew/Aramaic counterpart of the apkallū is the strongest scholarly cross-corpus link (Reed 2005; VanderKam 1984). The astrological-divination assignments here are the foundation of the Astronomical Book (1 En 72-82, Ship B). **LENS-RISK**: this is the second tier of the knowledge-transfer site (after v. 1 Asael); the text presents these as illicit/corrupting, but the canon engages them as 'foundational sciences' the Elohim taught humanity. Editor to handle.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ ἀπολλυμένων τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐβόησαν, καὶ ἡ φωνὴ αὐτῶν ἀνέβη εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.
verses.translit: Kai apollymenōn tōn anthrōpōn eboēsan, kai hē phōnē autōn anebē eis ton ouranon.
verses.text_geez: ወእንዘ፡ ይትኀጐሉ፡ ሰብእ፡ ጸርኁ፡ ወቃሎሙ፡ ዐርገ፡ ሰማየ፡
verses.notes: Humanity's cry rises to heaven — completes the earth-complaint pattern (7:6) and sets up the four archangels' intervention in 9:1ff. cf. Exod 2:23 (Israel's cry from Egypt).
